rule_statement: Hard data, role, safety, and grammar constraints determine whether a partial design can be completed.
scope: declared M4 chart grammar and typed IR roles
failure_condition: A required role is absent, safety requires abstention, or a chart is outside the versioned vocabulary.
conflict_policy: Hard failure cannot be offset by a soft preference score.

rule_statement: Task-specific chart families enumerate genuine alternative completions rather than one forced chart.
scope: supported core analytical tasks with complete typed field roles
failure_condition: Task is auxiliary, unresolved, or outside the supported core task set.
conflict_policy: Enumerate only templates whose required roles are satisfied.

rule_statement: Candidate encodings preserve raw and derived semantic roles, including fieldless row count, without inventing schema fields.
scope: field and encoding assignment from raw, aggregate-derived, and row-count VisualizationIntentIR roles
failure_condition: The requested encoding requires a field role absent from the IR.
conflict_policy: Retain distinct color/facet branches only when both are role-compatible.

rule_statement: Soft effectiveness preferences must remain componentized, source-scoped, and auditable.
scope: surviving hard-valid candidate completions
failure_condition: A score component or configured weight is missing.
conflict_policy: The fixed formula combines components; scores never override hard rejection.

rule_statement: Semantic-equivalent candidates must be deduplicated before ranking, and top-k must never be padded.
scope: all enumerated M4 candidate specifications
failure_condition: Canonical signature inputs are incomplete or nondeterministic.
conflict_policy: Keep one canonical representative per signature; never clone a survivor.

rule_statement: Variable-length output should preserve genuine chart-family, encoding, transform, and task diversity within a fixed budget.
scope: distinct hard-valid candidate set after deduplication
failure_condition: A diversity branch violates a hard constraint or only renames an identical encoding.
conflict_policy: Quality constraints dominate diversity; fewer candidates are valid.

rule_statement: A compatible explicit chart request constrains enumeration; an incompatible hint must remain visible instead of being silently replaced.
scope: explicit chart mentions that are compatible with the typed task and field roles
failure_condition: The explicit chart family is unsupported or role-incompatible.
conflict_policy: Compatible hint is a hard filter; incompatible hint yields zero executable candidates and a recorded reason.

rule_statement: A candidate must declare its data-grain operation; the planner uses a versioned unit-aware mean/sum policy instead of leaving M5 to reject an incomplete design.
scope: group-representing charts with mathematically certain duplicate group keys and no explicit aggregation
failure_condition: Measure units disagree or no grounded measure field is available.
conflict_policy: Explicit aggregation always wins; unknown or mixed units use the conservative mean policy and retain an audit assumption.

rule_statement: A typed fold prevents the planner from silently dropping all but the first requested measure in grouped comparison designs.
scope: multi-measure comparison over one grounded dimension
failure_condition: Fewer than two grounded quantitative fields or no comparison dimension is available.
conflict_policy: All folded source measures remain explicit; derived key/value fields are declared by the transform and checked by M5.

rule_statement: A candidate may choose among valid encodings but may not silently drop a grounded analytical field; filter-only fields remain in data scope without becoming visual grouping channels.
scope: required field-role obligations compiled from VisualizationIntentIR before chart-template completion
failure_condition: Any required field obligation is absent from the candidate data scope or assigned an incompatible role.
conflict_policy: Hard obligation completeness dominates chart score; candidates that cannot close the obligation are not emitted.

rule_statement: Transform semantics are part of the visualization plan contract and must survive template enumeration independently of chart ranking.
scope: typed filter, sort, time-unit, aggregation, limit, and fold obligations at the IntentIR-to-candidate boundary
failure_condition: A typed transform obligation is absent or materially altered in an emitted candidate.
conflict_policy: Explicit typed transforms dominate planner defaults; unresolved conflicts yield no executable candidate.

rule_statement: A typed candidate contract is a safety boundary. Construction failures must be auditable row-level rejections rather than process-wide exceptions.
scope: validate channel uniqueness per enumerated row and isolate a malformed candidate without aborting valid sibling candidates
failure_condition: One invalid candidate row aborts the full planning request or duplicate channels are silently repaired.
conflict_policy: Identical duplicate encodings are deduplicated; conflicting duplicate channels are rejected without guessing or channel reassignment; valid sibling rows continue.

rule_statement: Native chart labels and x/y orientation variants can encode the same common visualization plan; top-k must contain distinct decisions rather than nomenclature variants.
scope: retain one highest-scoring deterministic representative for candidates equivalent under common chart family, field set, encoding-role groups, aggregation, binning, time unit, and typed transforms
failure_condition: The candidate list contains multiple entries that normalize to the same common plan signature.
conflict_policy: Differences in fields, channel-role groups, aggregates, binning, temporal units, filters, or typed transforms preserve both candidates; ties use the native deterministic signature.

rule_statement: Explicit fields must not be replaced by schema-order defaults.
scope: explicit normalized field-name mentions
failure_condition: No complete field-name span occurs in the query.
conflict_policy: All exact collisions remain candidates.

rule_statement: User language may use a documented alternate field name.
scope: versioned aliases supplied with the dataset
failure_condition: Alias metadata is absent or the alias does not occur.
conflict_policy: Exact field names outrank aliases; alias collisions remain ambiguous.

rule_statement: A value mention can identify the field that supplies a filter or grouping dimension.
scope: exact casefolded matches to bounded profiled values
failure_condition: Value index is gated, missing or collides across fields.
conflict_policy: Every colliding field is retained with an ambiguity record.

rule_statement: Schema linking must be independent from chart construction.
scope: all M2 field resolution
failure_condition: A downstream chart hint is used as field evidence.
conflict_policy: Reject unregistered field evidence and never inject schema-order defaults.

rule_statement: Normalized field phrases should match common schema naming conventions and inflections.
scope: singular/plural, abbreviation-expanded, snake_case and camelCase field forms
failure_condition: Normalized token sets have no complete or near-complete correspondence.
conflict_policy: Exact lexical evidence outranks normalized evidence.

rule_statement: Natural language may omit modifiers from a column label.
scope: multi-token fields with non-trivial token overlap
failure_condition: Only generic tokens overlap or overlap is below the configured threshold.
conflict_policy: Token overlap cannot displace exact/alias evidence; ties remain candidates.

rule_statement: Semantic type provides a small compatibility signal, not permission to invent a field.
scope: already evidenced field candidates
failure_condition: Candidate has no lexical, alias or value evidence.
conflict_policy: Type compatibility cannot create a candidate on its own.

rule_statement: Task roles may rank fields while preserving the underlying evidence.
scope: already evidenced candidates with explicit task or operation hints
failure_condition: No task/operation evidence or no base field evidence.
conflict_policy: Task-role score is a small component and cannot override exact conflicts.

rule_statement: Required-field recovery preserves named fields and can expose a unique human-readable entity label as structural evidence.
scope: multi-field preservation, unresolved mentions, and unique label recovery for explicit each-entity structure
failure_condition: A mention has no candidate above threshold.
conflict_policy: Do not collapse different mentions into one field; unresolved mentions are explicit.

rule_statement: A bounded semantic bridge covers stable domain synonyms while preserving ties and a registry hash; it does not use embedding or LLM guesses.
scope: versioned query/schema concept pairs within the active single-table schema
failure_condition: No registered concept connects a query span to a schema field surface.
conflict_policy: All fields aligned through the same concept remain candidates and enter ordinary field ambiguity handling.

rule_statement: An entity noun in a row-count expression denotes the counted row population and must not become an unintended visual dimension.
scope: identifier-only partial matches governed by explicit row-count phrases
failure_condition: The match has stronger exact, alias, value, or grouping evidence.
conflict_policy: Retain the identifier candidate and evidence in the trace but exclude it from required visual fields.

rule_statement: Mentions must exist independently of any early commitment to a schema field.
scope: schema-independent semantic mentions with explicit query spans
failure_condition: A semantic concept is assigned without a query span.
conflict_policy: Overlapping mentions remain visible; longer and more specific concepts receive contrastive precedence.

rule_statement: A correct field must survive into joint reasoning before precision-oriented selection occurs.
scope: high-recall candidate generation from lexical, concept, value, schema-component, and role evidence
failure_condition: A candidate has no auditable query-to-schema evidence edge.
conflict_policy: Candidate generation maximizes bounded recall; it never selects by schema order.

rule_statement: A field is justified by why it fits better than nearby alternatives, not only by an isolated score.
scope: contrastive selection among semantically related fields in the same schema
failure_condition: A competing field is suppressed without positive and negative evidence.
conflict_policy: Specific entity-property evidence outranks generic type overlap; unresolved close alternatives remain ambiguous.

rule_statement: An exact schema-name match is evidence, not proof of an independent field reference; local syntax must distinguish 'profit values' from 'profit and value'.
scope: suppress a generic value/values field obligation when the token is an adjacent nominal head of another explicitly grounded field
failure_condition: A generic value field survives as an independent obligation despite an adjacent grounded measure with no coordination cue.
conflict_policy: Preserve the generic field candidate for audit, remove only its required obligation; explicit standalone or coordinated mentions remain required.

rule_statement: Schema semantic type and query role are distinct. A global by/across cue must not convert an aggregate operand into a grouping dimension when the cue locally modifies another field.
scope: resolve a physically numeric low-cardinality field as a query-local measure when an explicit aggregate operation binds to that field and no local grouping cue binds to it
failure_condition: A numeric aggregate operand is treated as a dimension because an unrelated grouping cue exists elsewhere in the query.
conflict_policy: Explicit operator-to-field binding outranks global grouping evidence; local grouping evidence on the same field blocks promotion; non-numeric fields are never promoted.

rule_statement: Token overlap is useful for recall but a shared schema token such as area must not create independent field obligations when it occurs only inside an explicitly grounded longer field phrase.
scope: remove a required-field obligation when its only lexical support is a schema-shared token already owned by a stronger complete field mention
failure_condition: One complete field mention expands into several unrelated required fields through a shared schema token.
conflict_policy: Independent exact, normalized, alias, acronym, semantic-concept, or value evidence preserves the field; only weak overlap evidence may be suppressed.

rule_statement: In phrases such as distribution of demand, distribution denotes an analytical task unless the similarly named schema field has independent strong evidence.
scope: separate an analytical-operation cue from a similarly named field when the remaining phrase is fully grounded by another explicit field
failure_condition: An analytical operation token is counted both as task evidence and as an independent required field.
conflict_policy: A complete exact or alias mention of the operation-named field wins; otherwise operation ownership plus an explicit base field suppresses only the weak obligation.

rule_statement: Lexical observations, schema-derived inferences, and task-conditioned compatibility have different epistemic force and must not be interchangeable in required-field decisions.
scope: classify every field-resolution evidence item as explicit grounding, semantic grounding, schema inference, contextual support, or weak overlap
failure_condition: A schema inference or contextual compatibility signal is treated as equivalent to a query-grounded field mention.
conflict_policy: The classification is immutable and auditable; it does not change candidate scores by itself and unknown evidence types default to contextual support.

rule_statement: A weak phrase window may cross two complete mentions, so ownership must be decided token by token rather than by requiring one owner span to contain the entire window.
scope: remove a required-field obligation only when all of its query-grounded token support is owned by one or more stronger explicit field mentions and no independent complete mention remains
failure_condition: A phrase such as convex area across grain class creates an extra grain-area obligation because a weak window combines tokens owned by convex-area and grain-class mentions.
conflict_policy: Any independent complete explicit, alias, acronym, value, or semantic mention preserves the obligation; schema inference and contextual support cannot defeat explicit multi-owner coverage.

rule_statement: In phrases such as customer segment groups, the trailing generic head labels the explicitly named grouping field and is not independent evidence for every schema field sharing that head.
scope: suppress a weak required-field obligation when every query-grounded token is a schema-shared head immediately following a stronger complete field mention that contains the same head
failure_condition: A trailing generic group/category/type/class/segment token promotes unrelated fields that only share the suffix.
conflict_policy: Any explicit, semantic, alias, value, or non-adjacent independent mention preserves the obligation; candidates remain in the audit contract.

rule_statement: Low-cardinality codes are often stored numerically but function as dimensions; query-local grammatical role is stronger than physical dtype for visualization planning.
scope: interpret a physically numeric explicitly grounded field as a categorical grouping role when local among/across/by/for or following group/category discourse marks it as the group key and no aggregate targets it
failure_condition: A numeric-coded group field in contrast mean X among Y categories is treated as a second measure, causing correlation or abstention.
conflict_policy: Typed aggregate-target evidence preserves the measure role; absent explicit field grounding or local grouping discourse prevents conversion.

rule_statement: Words such as mean, average, sum, and count denote analytical operations and must not independently ground schema fields that merely contain those tokens.
scope: remove a required-field obligation when all of its query-grounded evidence is weak token overlap wholly covered by typed operation evidence spans and the candidate has no independent explicit or semantic grounding
failure_condition: The aggregation word average adds capital_average when the query explicitly requests capital_total.
conflict_policy: Exact full-field, alias, value, acronym, or semantic grounding always preserves the field; candidates and raw evidence remain available for audit.

rule_statement: Longest lexical matching can create a false field such as mean_volume across the analytical operator mean and the real field volume_total; typed span ownership must precede field obligation emission.
scope: suppress a required candidate when every grounded span is either weak evidence owned by a normalized operation span or a false exact mention that decomposes into an operation span followed by the prefix of another independently exact full-field span
failure_condition: The phrase mean volume_total independently grounds both volume_total and schema field mean_volume.
conflict_policy: Standalone exact/alias/value/semantic evidence remains protected; decomposition requires an explicit typed operation and a distinct exact owner field with adjacent spans.

rule_statement: Ranking is a typed relation between entities and a score expression. Physical numeric type alone cannot distinguish a category code from the measure used to score it.
scope: bind an explicitly grounded numeric-coded field as a grouping dimension when it is the target of a rank/order directive and a distinct field is introduced after by, using, based on, or according to with an explicit aggregate
failure_condition: Rank cell_band using average cell_total is reduced to correlation because both fields are physically numeric.
conflict_policy: Do not convert a field without a grounded target span between the ranking directive and linkage phrase, a distinct grounded score field after the linkage, and an explicit aggregate operation.

rule_statement: A field's analytical role is query-dependent: explicit set discourse denotes grouping over distinct values even when the storage type is numeric.
scope: bind an explicitly grounded physically numeric field as a grouping dimension when an immediately following levels, tiers, strata, or buckets noun denotes the field's value set and the field is not an aggregate target
failure_condition: Comparing mean response between numeric category levels is reduced to a two-measure correlation or safe abstention.
conflict_policy: Requires strong field grounding and an adjacent plural set noun; aggregate-target fields, standalone level-named measures, and unmarked dual-quantitative relations are preserved.

rule_statement: Longest grounded schema mentions prevent a generic field from shadowing a more specific requested field while retaining auditable evidence.
scope: overlapping field mentions where a shorter field span is fully contained by a longer equally grounded field span of the same role
failure_condition: A shorter field is removed without complete span containment and equivalent or stronger grounding for the longer field.
conflict_policy: Do not collapse non-contained mentions or fields with distinct roles.

rule_statement: Auxiliary operations must decorate a visualization task instead of replacing it, and explicit sort/time-unit obligations must remain typed before planning.
scope: auxiliary filtering intent with grounded measure and display dimension, and supported lexical time-unit or ranking obligations
failure_condition: A visualization task or transform is introduced without grounded fields and direct query evidence.
conflict_policy: Existing typed task and transform declarations always win; the compiler only closes a uniquely determined obligation.

rule_statement: Roles are arrays and relations, not scalar x/y/color slots.
scope: multi-field VisualizationIntentIR roles
failure_condition: Field evidence is missing or below threshold.
conflict_policy: Preserve all supported roles and explicit role ambiguity.

rule_statement: Equivalent evidence must serialize identically and variable candidates must not be cloned.
scope: deterministic IR candidate ordering and identity
failure_condition: Input order is nondeterministic or duplicate candidates are present.
conflict_policy: Sort by score, rank and stable names; deduplicate only exact semantic duplicates.

rule_statement: Every semantic decision must expose both its evidence and constraint path.
scope: typed graph connecting query spans, schema fields, roles, goals, operations, and presentation hints
failure_condition: A selected field, role, task, or operation lacks a graph edge to evidence or a rule.
conflict_policy: Missing proof paths prevent an interpretation from being marked complete.

rule_statement: Low local confidence must not terminate a query when global constraints can identify a unique safe interpretation.
scope: delayed abstention after complete hypothesis enumeration
failure_condition: The pipeline abstains before bounded complete hypotheses are checked.
conflict_policy: Unsupported scope and material ambiguity still dominate coverage recovery.

rule_statement: Transform obligations are part of semantic correctness.
scope: registered aggregate, filter, bin, sort, limit and time-unit expressions
failure_condition: Operation is neither explicit nor one of the registered implicit-count constructions.
conflict_policy: Conflicting operations remain separate transforms and raise ambiguity.

rule_statement: Measures, groups, time and filters must remain distinct.
scope: resolved field candidates with explicit or structural roles
failure_condition: Field role evidence is absent or conflicting.
conflict_policy: Retain multiple roles when evidence is tied; never overwrite an upstream candidate.

rule_statement: Filter polarity, temporal scope and limits cannot be reconstructed after they are dropped.
scope: explicit filter values, negation, time scopes and numeric top/bottom limits
failure_condition: Attachment between expression and field is unresolved.
conflict_policy: Record unresolved attachment or alternatives instead of guessing.

rule_statement: Threshold language must compile into a typed filter and must not leak into ranking or extremum detection.
scope: inclusive numeric threshold phrases such as at least and at most
failure_condition: The numeric threshold cannot be attached to a grounded quantitative or ordinal field.
conflict_policy: Unattached thresholds remain material ambiguity; they are never converted to rank direction.

rule_statement: Compact and synonymous chart tokens must remain explicit downstream evidence.
scope: registered English chart tokens and aliases
failure_condition: Token is not in the registered vocabulary or collides with a schema term.
conflict_policy: Preserve the original token and record the canonical alternative; never delete the source span.

rule_statement: Planning stages require explicit operation hints rather than a single keyword-to-chart decision.
scope: registered task, temporal, aggregation, ranking and channel phrases
failure_condition: Phrase is outside the versioned vocabulary.
conflict_policy: Retain all detected compatible hints; conflicting hints become explicit evidence, not priority overwrite.

rule_statement: Equivalent surface forms need stable matching while original evidence remains recoverable.
scope: Unicode, case and whitespace normalization
failure_condition: Input is empty or not a string.
conflict_policy: Original text and per-token spans are authoritative.

rule_statement: Equivalent surface forms should share lexical evidence without changing the observed query span.
scope: bounded inflections, schema abbreviations, snake_case and camelCase field forms
failure_condition: Normalization is outside the registered morphology or abbreviation vocabulary.
conflict_policy: Lemmas are auxiliary; normalized query keeps the observed token.

rule_statement: Ranking and extremum intent depends on degree and limit evidence.
scope: registered comparative, superlative, top and bottom expressions
failure_condition: Comparative expression is outside the registered vocabulary.
conflict_policy: Opposing directions are both retained and later marked ambiguous.

rule_statement: Filters and exclusions lose meaning if negation is removed.
scope: registered negation and limitation tokens
failure_condition: Token is outside the registered vocabulary.
conflict_policy: Never drop negation; attach it only to an explicit filter during decomposition.

rule_statement: Residual surface tokens are non-material only when they cannot alter a task, role, constraint, or capability decision.
scope: impact-aware residual tokens after task, role, and typed-transform obligations are complete
failure_condition: A residue token changes a required field, task, operation, threshold, or relation.
conflict_policy: Material impact takes precedence over lexical-residue classification.

rule_statement: Planning safety depends on distinguishing missing obligations and real semantic alternatives from lexical noise.
scope: material qualifiers, unrepresented constraints, missing task roles, and surviving interpretation alternatives
failure_condition: No evidence span or affected semantic object can be identified.
conflict_policy: Missing required roles outrank material qualifiers; material qualifiers outrank multiple valid interpretations.

rule_statement: A valid field does not imply that the requested governing operation is supported.
scope: versioned capability vocabulary after analytical task profiling
failure_condition: The governing operation is outside both the supported and unsupported versioned vocabularies.
conflict_policy: Any explicit unsupported governing operation dominates supported structural fallback tasks.

rule_statement: Unsupported requests must terminate before candidate planning instead of yielding a plausible but unsafe visualization task.
scope: capability assessments containing one or more unsupported operations
failure_condition: Unsupported operation evidence is absent.
conflict_policy: Force semantic-safety abstention and retain upstream task candidates only as diagnostic evidence.

rule_statement: Capability checking must preserve supported descriptive visualization tasks and avoid false abstention.
scope: queries with no detected unsupported governing operation
failure_condition: An unsupported governing operation or an upstream failure is present.
conflict_policy: Do not change upstream fields, tasks, or transforms; safety may only type ambiguity or abstain.

rule_statement: The same token can denote an operation or a measured attribute; schema-grounded field evidence must be checked before a capability gate treats it as a governing operation.
scope: capability lexemes whose complete evidence span is grounded inside a schema field mention
failure_condition: A lexeme is suppressed without a stronger exact, alias, normalized, or semantic-concept field span that contains it.
conflict_policy: A separate governing verb or future/intervention cue dominates field-span precedence; otherwise the grounded field interpretation is retained.

rule_statement: Forecast and prediction are related but distinct requested operations; an explicit predict verb must not be relabeled as forecast merely because future scope is also present.
scope: map unsupported governing-operation lexemes to a versioned canonical label while preserving the matched lexical form and span
failure_condition: A query safely abstains but reports a canonical unsupported-operation label inconsistent with its governing verb.
conflict_policy: Explicit forecast lexemes map to forecast; explicit predict lexemes map to prediction even with future modifiers; project plus future scope maps to forecast; field-grounded spans are excluded before classification.

rule_statement: Cross-schema grounding requires field structure beyond a flat token bag.
scope: versioned decomposition of schema field names into entity, property, qualifier, and type concepts
failure_condition: No registered or lexical schema component can be recovered.
conflict_policy: Preserve every compatible concept and defer selection to contrastive field resolution.

rule_statement: Physical dtype and visualization semantic type are distinct; value-shape evidence can recover legacy temporal columns.
scope: single-table physical/semantic typing including parseable timestamps and bounded year-valued fields
failure_condition: Field has no non-null values and no reliable physical type evidence.
conflict_policy: Retain physical dtype and emit semantic unknown when evidence conflicts.

rule_statement: Observed values may ground query mentions to fields.
scope: bounded low-cardinality value anchors under the configured access policy
failure_condition: Value matching is disabled, cardinality exceeds the bound, or samples are unavailable.
conflict_policy: Colliding values remain candidates for every matching field.

rule_statement: Role compatibility cannot be inferred from column name alone.
scope: cardinality, null rate and value distribution profiling
failure_condition: Data values are unavailable.
conflict_policy: Profile missing statistics explicitly; do not invent defaults.

rule_statement: Temporal roles require value/dtype evidence and should not rely only on field names.
scope: datetime dtype or date-like value evidence
failure_condition: Date parse evidence is weak or based only on a name token.
conflict_policy: Weak name evidence produces a warning or unknown; dtype/value evidence controls the decision.

rule_statement: Special semantic types need value-distribution evidence in addition to names.
scope: identifier, ordinal and geographic classification with multiple evidence signals
failure_condition: Only a name hint is present or evidence families disagree.
conflict_policy: Prefer unknown/categorical and record a warning rather than force a special type.

rule_statement: Physical string type does not determine visualization semantic type; timestamp morphology is positive evidence even when a producer omits the separator between an ISO date and time.
scope: infer a temporal semantic type from a bounded column sample when at least 80 percent of non-null strings match a registered calendar or timestamp morphology and at least two distinct values parse
failure_condition: A date or timestamp column is treated as categorical solely because its serialized representation is non-standard but deterministically parseable.
conflict_policy: Existing temporal types win; numeric identifiers are excluded; morphology and parse thresholds must both pass; profiling never rewrites source values.

rule_statement: Lexical tokens such as time can denote a duration measure; explicit aggregate-role evidence is stronger than a field-name temporal hint.
scope: restore a physically numeric field to quantitative when a typed aggregate explicitly targets it and no value-shape temporal profile exists
failure_condition: A numeric duration such as handling_time is converted into a temporal dimension despite being the explicit target of mean, sum, or median.
conflict_policy: Value-shape temporal evidence or an existing temporal summary prevents restoration; min/max temporal extrema are left unchanged.

rule_statement: Field-name hints are weak schema evidence. For a relationship task, typed task evidence and numeric value shape should dominate a suffix such as time when the values do not parse as temporal data.
scope: restore a required, physically numeric field from a lexical temporal-name hint to a quantitative query-local role when explicit correlation discourse binds it to another numeric field and neither value-shape nor trend discourse supports a temporal interpretation
failure_condition: A numeric measure named time_value is treated as a temporal axis in a query such as plot time_value against monetary_value.
conflict_policy: Do not apply when the query contains trend discourse, the field has a temporal value summary, fewer than two required numeric-shaped fields are grounded, or the field lacks strong query grounding.

rule_statement: Minimum and maximum can summarize numeric duration measures. A lexical time token is weaker than numeric value shape plus an explicit aggregate-target and grouping relation.
scope: restore a physically numeric field from a weak temporal-name role to quantitative when an explicit grouped min/max aggregation targets it, a distinct grouping dimension is grounded, and no temporal value summary or trend discourse exists
failure_condition: Minimum wait_time by desk is encoded as a temporal axis and rejected despite numeric values and an explicit grouped aggregate.
conflict_policy: Any parsed temporal value summary, datetime physical type, missing grouping dimension, absent explicit aggregate target, or trend discourse prevents restoration.

rule_statement: Task candidates require operational semantics separate from chart type.
scope: declared SkillVIS v2 analytical task vocabulary
failure_condition: Intent is outside the declared task vocabulary.
conflict_policy: Compatible primary and secondary tasks coexist.

rule_statement: Task inference combines query, schema, and derived-measure evidence; a chart token alone remains insufficient.
scope: task inference from explicit chart evidence, schema roles, and raw or derived analytical measures
failure_condition: A required chart/task role lacks grounded raw or derived field evidence.
conflict_policy: Explicit incompatible task remains a separate candidate.

rule_statement: Insufficient evidence should produce alternatives or unresolved state, not a forced default.
scope: underspecified one- or multi-field requests
failure_condition: Explicit task evidence resolves the interpretation.
conflict_policy: Retain tied plausible tasks and mark task ambiguity.

rule_statement: Explicit task language is direct evidence but must not directly choose a chart.
scope: registered explicit analytical task phrases
failure_condition: No registered task phrase occurs.
conflict_policy: Multiple explicit task phrases become multiple scored candidates.

rule_statement: Superlatives imply ranking direction and often a bounded extremum result.
scope: ranking, extremum and top/bottom expressions
failure_condition: Degree/direction evidence is absent.
conflict_policy: Opposing directions produce ambiguity; do not select one silently.

rule_statement: Aggregation, filtering, and sorting describe means; they must not replace the analytical goal.
scope: separation of analytical goal, data operations, and presentation intent
failure_condition: An auxiliary operation is emitted as the primary analytical goal.
conflict_policy: A structurally complete core analytical goal dominates auxiliary operations.

rule_statement: Task words are only valid when their required field and operation structure can be executed.
scope: hard role and arity constraints for core analytical goals
failure_condition: A task survives despite a hard role or arity violation.
conflict_policy: Hard structural constraints dominate lexical task cues and chart hints.

rule_statement: Global semantic consistency is more reliable than independent local classifications.
scope: composition and deterministic ranking of complete field-task-operation hypotheses
failure_condition: A selected interpretation does not close all required roles and operations.
conflict_policy: Complete hypotheses outrank incomplete hypotheses; soft scores never override hard violations.

rule_statement: Ambiguity is material only when multiple executable interpretations differ in core semantics.
scope: material ambiguity after structural hypothesis validation
failure_condition: Lexical residue alone creates a competing executable interpretation.
conflict_policy: Preserve close complete alternatives; otherwise select the uniquely best complete hypothesis.

rule_statement: Ranking is an analytical goal, whereas sorting is its execution operation; an explicit ranking directive must not fall back to generic comparison.
scope: compile an explicit rank/ranking directive into a ranking analytical goal when dimension and measure roles are structurally complete
failure_condition: An executable explicit ranking request is selected as comparison, or ranking is forced without both measure and dimension roles.
conflict_policy: Explicit structurally complete ranking outranks comparison; incomplete ranking remains unresolved or is handled by existing safe ambiguity logic.

rule_statement: Ranking is a specific analytical goal that entails comparison; emitting both as peer predictions harms typed task precision and obscures the primary intent.
scope: promote field-unowned rank/order/sort directives only after measure-dimension closure and remove generic comparison from the emitted task candidate set while retaining the alternative hypothesis in the audit graph
failure_condition: An explicit order or sort request falls back to comparison, or an explicit rank request emits generic comparison as a peer task.
conflict_policy: Directive spans owned by field mentions are excluded; order/sort require an aggregation and a following by-clause; missing structural roles forbid promotion.

rule_statement: Analytical discourse and presentation evidence jointly disambiguate structurally complete tasks that bare field-count heuristics misclassify.
scope: promote contrast plus typed aggregation and grouping closure to comparison, or share/proportion plus explicit pie presentation and a single grouping field to composition
failure_condition: Contrast-with-aggregation is emitted as correlation, or explicit record proportions in a pie chart is emitted as distribution.
conflict_policy: Correlation cues without aggregation are preserved; composition requires explicit part-to-whole wording plus explicit pie presentation; alternative hypotheses stay in the audit graph.

rule_statement: A task decision should be closed from the typed target-score relation even when a surface ranking synonym is absent from the normalization lexicon.
scope: emit ranking as the sole analytical task when a rank/order directive is supported by an R-FR-120 target dimension, a distinct quantitative score field, and an explicit aggregate
failure_condition: Order tier_value according to average quality_total has correct field roles but remains a generic comparison.
conflict_policy: Requires the independently traced R-FR-120 role binding, a complete dimension-measure structure, and aggregation; it cannot fire from a rank/order token alone.

rule_statement: Ranking direction and score aggregation are orthogonal transforms. An explicit mean, median, sum, min, or max defines the score; direction language orders those scores and must not invent a second aggregate.
scope: treat highest-to-lowest, lowest-to-highest, largest-first, smallest-first, ascending, and descending language as ordering direction when a ranking relation already contains one explicit aggregate score operation
failure_condition: Rank groups by average score from highest to lowest emits both mean and max, leaving no singular aggregation and causing validator rejection.
conflict_policy: Requires a closed ranking task, a single explicit aggregate from the normalized query, and an unambiguous direction phrase; explicit max/min remains the aggregate and non-ranking superlative questions are unchanged.

rule_statement: A ranking request is a relation among entity target, aggregate score, and ordering direction; closing those roles jointly prevents direction words from being mistaken for a second aggregate and removes entailed comparison/extremum peer labels.
scope: close ranking from an explicit rank/order target-link-score relation, one explicit score aggregation, typed dimension and measure roles, and an unambiguous order-direction phrase before generic grouped-superlative interpretation can dominate
failure_condition: Order vendors by median cost from smallest to largest remains comparison, or ranking is emitted together with extremum.
conflict_policy: Requires distinct strongly grounded target and score fields, an explicit aggregation targeting the score, a recognized linkage phrase, and exactly one direction; missing roles or non-ranking superlatives remain unchanged.

rule_statement: AGGREGATION_OBLIGATION_MISMATCH
scope: Explicit IntentIR aggregation obligation.
failure_condition: IntentIR contains an aggregation.
conflict_policy: intent and candidate operations, fields, and transforms.

rule_statement: AGGREGATION_INTERNAL_MISMATCH
scope: Candidate aggregation, transforms, and aggregate encodings.
failure_condition: Candidate declares an aggregation.
conflict_policy: declared aggregation, matching transform count, and encoding aggregate values.

rule_statement: TRANSFORM_OBLIGATION_MISSING
scope: IntentIR filter, sort, and limit obligations.
failure_condition: IntentIR declares one or more non-aggregation transforms.
conflict_policy: canonical intent and candidate transform signatures.

rule_statement: DATA_GRAIN_CONFLICT
scope: Group-representing charts with mathematically certain duplicate grouping rows.
failure_condition: row_count exceeds the product of encoded grouping-key cardinalities.
conflict_policy: row count, grouping fields, cardinalities, chart scope, and aggregation absence.

rule_statement: CONTEXT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH
scope: SchemaProfile, VisualizationIntentIR, CapabilityAssessment, and candidate-set identity.
failure_condition: A formal validation context is supplied.
conflict_policy: dataset IDs, capability hashes, candidate IDs, ranks, and signatures.

rule_statement: ENCODING_TYPE_MISMATCH
scope: Encoding channel and schema semantic type.
failure_condition: Encoding field exists in schema.
conflict_policy: channel, field, declared type, schema type, and encoding-type matrix entry.

rule_statement: MARK_CHART_MISMATCH
scope: Chart type and mark.
failure_condition: Chart type belongs to the formal grammar.
conflict_policy: observed chart/mark and required formal mark.

rule_statement: REQUIRED_CHANNEL_MISSING
scope: Required channels for each formal chart type.
failure_condition: Chart and mark are in the formal grammar.
conflict_policy: observed channels and frozen required-channel set.

rule_statement: ENCODING_TYPE_MISMATCH
scope: Scatter and grouped-scatter axes.
failure_condition: Candidate chart is scatter or grouped_scatter.
conflict_policy: x/y fields and schema semantic types.

rule_statement: FIELD_NOT_IN_SCHEMA
scope: All candidate fields, encodings, and transforms.
failure_condition: SchemaProfile is valid.
conflict_policy: referenced field and complete schema field-name set.

rule_statement: FIELD_ROLE_MISMATCH
scope: Candidate measure roles.
failure_condition: Referenced measure exists in schema.
conflict_policy: candidate measure, schema semantic type, and IntentIR measure role.

rule_statement: FIELD_ROLE_MISMATCH
scope: Dimension, temporal, grouping, color, size, and facet roles.
failure_condition: Referenced role field exists in schema.
conflict_policy: candidate role assignment, schema semantic type, and matching IntentIR role.

rule_statement: PERCEPTUAL_EFFECTIVENESS_WARNING
scope: Pie angle/area comparison.
failure_condition: Candidate chart is pie and no hard rule is required for this concern.
conflict_policy: chart, task, encodings, and source scope.

rule_statement: HIGH_CARDINALITY_WARNING
scope: Pie, color, series, and facet encodings using SchemaProfile cardinality.
failure_condition: Encoded field cardinality exceeds a frozen threshold.
conflict_policy: schema field cardinality, channel, threshold, and config version.

rule_statement: ENCODING_OVERLOAD_WARNING
scope: Candidate encoding and auxiliary-channel counts.
failure_condition: Frozen count threshold is exceeded.
conflict_policy: encoding count, auxiliary channels, and threshold.

rule_statement: DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE_WARNING
scope: Complete candidate set.
failure_condition: Two candidates share a deterministic signature.
conflict_policy: candidate IDs and duplicate signatures.

rule_statement: CANDIDATE_SET_EXHAUSTED
scope: Complete validated candidate set.
failure_condition: Every candidate is rejected.
conflict_policy: all candidate decisions and violated hard rules.

rule_statement: TASK_CHART_MISMATCH
scope: Candidate task_alignment and chart type.
failure_condition: Task is represented in the formal compatibility matrix.
conflict_policy: task, chart, allowed chart set, and IntentIR task candidates.

rule_statement: UNSUPPORTED_DESIGN
scope: Candidate executable/audit-only/unsupported/rejection state and formal grammar.
failure_condition: Candidate reaches M5.
conflict_policy: candidate state and formal chart/mark/channel vocabulary.

rule_statement: SAFETY_BYPASS
scope: CapabilityAssessment and IntentIR abstention pass-through.
failure_condition: Capability requires abstention or IntentIR is abstained.
conflict_policy: unsupported operations, risk, abstention state, and surviving candidate.
